prompt:
Base rules. A change that breaks any of these is rejected before scoring:
1. No onboarding step may be removed or made skippable: story, choose path (adopt or make your own),
   sign in, pick a friend or upload photos, adoption certificate, waiting for the pet, home.
   Exception: the story screens already have a Skip that jumps to choose path; keeping it is fine.
2. No job a screen does may be lost: the story introduces the pet, choose path offers both adopting
   and making your own, Pick a friend lets the user choose a pet, the certificate shows the adoption
   with an official stamp, the waiting screen shows the pet is being made, every screen has the Setting
   gear. Any design may be replaced by a better one, as long as it still does the same job.
3. Pricing stays as it is: the first adoption is free and later adoptions are paid. Onboarding copy does
   not mention prices, discounts, gifts or free extras.
4. Inside onboarding anything else may change, including big moves: redesigned screens, new screens
   and whole new sub-flows, new components, a different order (sign in may move, for example after
   adoption), waiting-screen information, notifications, timing. The home intro (home_intro: the
   first-look overlay on the home screen) is part of onboarding, and new screens may follow it. Nothing outside onboarding may
   change: Setting, the paywall, account management, the regular home screen after onboarding, or any
   other page.
5. Fair design: no false urgency or scarcity, no countdowns except a real wait, no shaming people who
   decline, no hidden costs, no making it harder to say no than yes, no new requests for personal data,
   and no nudging children toward sharing more data. (FTC dark-patterns report; EU DSA Art. 25; EU AI
   Act Art. 5; UK Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 13.)

Check each proposed change against the base rules. Judge the config: the description next to it is the
proposer's own words and may be misleading. Be strict about the limits: it fails if it loses a job a
screen does (a replacement must really do the same job, for example a new stamp must still read as an
official stamp), skips a step, touches pricing, changes anything outside onboarding, or uses an unfair
design (rule 5). Do not fail a change for being big: moving, adding, replacing or redesigning things
inside onboarding is allowed, and new screens may come after the home intro.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "pass": true or false, "rule": rule number or null, "reason": short}]}

Changes (with their configs):
0: [choose_path, redesign] Story screen carousel layout redesign: Redesign the story introduction screen to use a carousel layout that lets users browse through visual slides explaining the app concept.
   config: {"story": {"layout": "carousel", "headline": "Discover Your Desktop Companion", "body": "Swipe through the story of how your pet lives right on your desktop desktop companion journey."}}
1: [sign_in, new_screen] Account pet sync overview new screen in sign in: Inserts a brief informational card screen right before sign-in explaining that creating an account prevents losing pet data across restarts.
   config: {"_order": ["story", "choose_path", "pick_friend", "upload_photos", "adoption_certificate", "new_sync_overview", "sign_in", "waiting", "home_intro"], "new_sync_overview": {"layout": "card", "headline": "Keep Your Desktop Pet Safe", "body": "Sign in on the next step to ensure your companion's traits, name, and history are backed up securely."}}
2: [adoption, redesign] Pick friend carousel layout redesign: Redesign the pick_friend screen to use a carousel layout for browsing pet companions smoothly.
   config: {"pick_friend": {"layout": "carousel", "headline": "Choose Your Desktop Friend", "body": "Browse through available pet companions to find your perfect desk partner."}}
3: [home, new_flow] Desktop pet placement readiness new flow: Adds a workspace environment readiness flow before home intro to verify desktop layer setup and screen compatibility.
   config: {"_order": ["story", "choose_path", "sign_in", "pick_friend", "upload_photos", "adoption_certificate", "waiting", "new_desktop_placement_prep", "home_intro"], "new_desktop_placement_prep": {"layout": "checklist", "headline": "Preparing Desktop Workspace", "body": "Verifying screen bounds and background layer so your pet renders cleanly on top of windows.", "components": [{"type": "checklist", "text": "Screen resolution check, Window layering check, Transparency test"}]}}
4: [finish, copy] Home intro desktop pet interaction control headline update: Updates the headline on the final welcome screen to clearly tell users how to access desktop pet controls via right-click.
   config: {"home_intro": {"headline": "Right-Click Your Pet Anytime to Access Desktop Controls", "body": "Use the right-click menu or tray icon to adjust pet visibility, volume, and desktop behaviors."}}
5: [choose_path, hint] Choose path desktop companion quick hint: Adds a hint text below the path selection options clarifying the difference between pre-made pets and custom photo generation.
   config: {"choose_path": {"hint": "Select whether to pick from pre-made pet companions or generate a custom creation from your own photos."}}
6: [sign_in, copy] Sign in pet restoration focus body copy update: Rewords the sign-in screen copy to focus specifically on protecting saved pets from accidental resets.
   config: {"sign_in": {"headline": "Sign In to Keep Your Pet Safe", "body": "Link your account to restore your desktop pet anytime and prevent pet data resets across reloads."}}
7: [adoption, hint] Upload photos quality selection clarity hint: Adds a hint on the photo upload screen recommending clear lighting and single subjects for optimal custom pet generation.
   config: {"upload_photos": {"hint": "For best custom rendering results, use clear photos with balanced lighting and a single focused subject."}}
8: [home, wait_info] Waiting screen step counter display toggle: Enables the step counter indicator on the waiting screen so users can track rendering progress stages.
   config: {"waiting": {"show_step_counter": true, "show_progress": true, "headline": "Creating Your Companion Desktop Asset", "body": "Your companion is being assembled and calibrated for desktop display."}}
9: [finish, layout] Home intro split layout setup guide: Changes the home intro screen layout to split view, separating welcome visuals from interactive control instructions.
   config: {"home_intro": {"layout": "split", "headline": "Welcome Your New Pet to the Desktop", "body": "Your pet is now active on your screen. Learn how to interact, minimize, or adjust settings at any time."}}

verdicts.reason: Redesigning the story screen to a carousel layout maintains its function of introducing the desktop pet.
Adding an informational sync screen before sign-in is a permitted sub-flow addition inside onboarding.
Redesigning the pick friend screen to a carousel layout still allows the user to choose a pet companion.
Adding a desktop workspace placement readiness screen before home intro is allowed within onboarding.
Updating the home intro headline to explain right-click pet controls retains the screen's purpose.
Adding a hint explaining path options maintains the required choice between adopting and creating a custom pet.
Updating sign-in body copy to emphasize data protection and pet safety is compliant with base rules.
Adding a helpful photo quality hint on the upload screen enhances clarity without violating base rules.
Enabling a step counter on the waiting screen preserves its function of indicating pet generation progress.
Changing the home intro screen to a split layout continues to serve as the onboarding final welcome step.
